reason: Selected confidence probe and limitations support calibrating stopping signals, without treating self-confirmation as independent verification.

candidates.title: Calibrate confidence before using it to stop reasoning
candidates.rule: Before using a model’s declared numeric confidence as an early-stop gate, test whether it separates correct and incorrect first attempts on the target workload.
candidates.passage: the backbone reports high confidence on essentially all first generations
candidates.location: Section 5.2, Experiment E6 limitations and conclusion
candidates.finding: The confidence-threshold sweep is overconfident and collapses tested high-threshold gates to single-shot behavior. The calibration recommendation is inferred; the paper instead uses a CONFIRMED sentinel for its bounded loop.
candidates.conditions: Frozen API backbones and pure-reasoning tasks. Independently repeated BBH anchors differ by about seven points in single-shot accuracy.
candidates.limitations: Self-confirmation is not external proof of correctness. Tool-use and multi-agent training are unevaluated blueprints. Session-sensitive estimates and small BBH sample limit stable threshold claims.
candidates.validation_test: Measure calibration and selective accuracy on held-out labeled tasks; compare fixed depth, confidence-based and other stopping policies at the same total budget, including premature stops.

review_scope: Selected abstract, introduction, methods or main-result sections; not a comprehensive paper or appendix review.
